flags: Central Garden & Pet divested its pet distribution business (fiscal 2025 net sales of $474 million) to a new partnership with Phillips Pet Food & Supplies, contributing net assets of approximately $57 million including inventory of approximately $69 million, and receiving approximately $31 million in cash, a $5 million note receivable, and a 20% ownership interest valued at $26 million, recognizing a pre-tax gain of $2.5 million.

Central Garden & Pet announced a definitive agreement to acquire approximately 80% of TRIXIE Heimtierbedarf GmbH & Co. KG, the leading European pet supplies and pet snacks company, for total consideration of up to €400 million (upfront €340 million cash plus earn-out of up to €60.0 million), subject to regulatory approval, with closing expected in the first half of fiscal 2027.

Central Garden & Pet raised its fiscal 2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS outlook from $2.70 or better to $2.85 or better, citing continued margin discipline, ongoing investment in growth initiatives, and portfolio optimization.

business_model.claim: Central Garden & Pet operates through two reportable segments: Pet and Garden.
quotes: We operate through two reportable segments: Pet and Garden.

business_model.claim: The Pet segment sells dog and cat supplies (treats, chews, toys, beds, containment, grooming, waste management), aquatics, small animal, reptile and pet bird supplies, equine and livestock products, live fish and small animals, and outdoor cushions under brands including Nylabone, Kaytee, Farnam, Aqueon, Comfort Zone and Zoëcon.
quotes: Our Pet segment offers a broad range of products for dog and cat supplies, including treats and chews, toys, beds and containment, grooming items, waste management and training pads. We also provide supplies for aquatics, small animals, reptiles and pet birds, such as toys, enclosures, habitats, bedding, food and supplements, equine and livestock products, animal and household health solutions and insect control items.

business_model.claim: The Garden segment sells grass seed, vegetable/flower/herb packet seed, wild bird feed, bird houses, herbicides, insecticide and pesticide products, fertilizers and live plants under brands including Pennington, Amdro, Ferry-Morse, Sevin and 3D.
quotes: Our Garden segment includes lawn and garden consumables such as grass seed; vegetable, flower and herb packet seed; wild bird feed, bird houses and other birding accessories; weed, grass, and other herbicides, insecticide and pesticide products; fertilizers and live plants.

business_model.claim: In fiscal 2025 consolidated net sales were $3.1 billion, with the Pet segment contributing approximately $1.8 billion and the Garden segment approximately $1.3 billion.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, our consolidated net sales were $3.1 billion, of which our Pet segment, or Pet, accounted for approximately $1.8 billion and our Garden segment, or Garden, accounted for approximately $1.3 billion.

business_model.claim: The company sells through major national retailers, independent pet specialty stores, mass merchants, farm-and-feed outlets and online channels; Walmart, Home Depot, Costco, Lowe's and Amazon together accounted for approximately 54% of total net sales in fiscal 2025.
quotes: Together with Costco, Lowe's and Amazon these major retailers represented approximately 54% of total net sales in fiscal 2025 and 2024.

business_model.claim: In fiscal 2025, branded product sales represented approximately 79% of net sales and sales of other manufacturers' products represented 21%.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, sales of branded products represented approximately 79% of our net sales, compared to 78% in fiscal 2024, and sales of other manufacturers' products represented 21% of our net sales.

business_model.claim: Q3 fiscal 2026 GAAP net sales fell 8.2% to $882.4 million versus $960.9 million a year earlier, driven by the divestiture of the pet distribution business, while organic net sales (excluding divestitures, UK closure and the Champion acquisition) increased 2.4%.
quotes: Net sales for the three months ended June 27, 2026, decreased $78.5 million, or 8.2%, to $882.4 million from $960.9 million for the three months ended June 28, 2025. Organic net sales for the quarter ended June 27, 2026, which excludes the impact of the divestiture of the pet distribution business divested in April 2026, the closure of our operations in the United Kingdom during fiscal 2025 and the acquisition of Champion in December 2025, increased 2.4% from the prior year quarter.

business_model.claim: Garden segment Q3 fiscal 2026 net sales increased 2.9% to $481.9 million from $468.4 million, driven by volume-based increases in wild bird feed, controls and grass seed from increased retailer listings.
quotes: Garden net sales increased $13.5 million, or 2.9%, to $481.9 million for the three months ended June 27, 2026, from $468.4 million for the three months ended June 28, 2025. The increase in Garden net sales was due primarily to increased sales in wild bird feed, controls and grass seed businesses, primarily volume-based increases from increased retailer listings.

business_model.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
business_model.claim: The Garden business is highly seasonal: in fiscal 2025, approximately 64% of Garden segment net sales and 57% of total net sales occurred during the second and third fiscal quarters, and substantially all Garden operating income is generated in that period.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, approximately 64% of our Garden segment's net sales and 57% of our total net sales occurred during our second and third fiscal quarters. Substantially all of the Garden segment's operating income is generated in this period.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P4 and P8
business_model.claim: Revenue is also driven by M&A and divestitures: Central has completed more than 60 acquisitions since 1992, divested its pet distribution business in April 2026 (fiscal 2025 net sales $474 million), and agreed in July 2026 to acquire approximately 80% of TRIXIE, the leading European pet supplies and pet snacks company, for up to €400 million.
quotes: Since 1992, we have completed more than 60 acquisitions, building a company with approximately $3.1 billion in net sales.
Pet Distribution's net sales in fiscal 2025 were $474 million.

the Company will pay a total consideration of up to €400 million, with an upfront consideration of approximately €340 million paid in cash at closing and an earn-out potential of up to €60.0 million based on 2026 performance

business_model.claim: Gross margin in Q3 fiscal 2026 was 35.9%, up 130 basis points from 34.6% a year earlier, driven by the exit of the lower-margin pet distribution business and cost and simplicity initiatives in both segments.
quotes: Gross margin increased 130 basis points to 35.9% for the three months ended June 27, 2026 from 34.6% for the three months ended June 28, 2025.

At the same time, gross margin improved due primarily to both the positive impact of the divestiture of our pet distribution business, which had lower margins, and our cost and simplicity initiatives in both segments.

business_model.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
business_model.claim: Cost of goods sold is exposed to commodity seed and grain prices, energy costs, and U.S. import tariffs; in fiscal 2025, less than 15% of COGS was from products or materials sourced outside the United States, primarily from China, Brazil and Mexico.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, less than 15% of our cost of goods sold was from products or materials sourced from outside the United States, primarily from China, Brazil and Mexico.
Seeds and grains we use to produce bird feed and grass seed are commodity products subject to price volatility that could have a negative impact on us.

business_model.claim: The company manufactures the majority of its branded products in U.S.-based facilities, supplemented by contract manufacturing (including an exclusive supply of its registered active ingredient (S)-Methoprene) and manufacturing facilities in Canada and Mexico.
quotes: We manufacture the majority of our branded products in our U.S.-based facilities, supplemented by select contract manufacturing arrangements, including an exclusive supply of our registered active ingredient (S)-Methoprene. In addition, we operate manufacturing facilities in Canada and Mexico.

business_model.claim: Customer concentration is high: Walmart accounted for approximately 17% of fiscal 2025 net sales and Home Depot for approximately 16%, with the loss of or adverse change in any key retailer relationship posing a material risk to sales and cash flow.
quotes: Walmart, our largest customer, accounted for approximately 17% of total net sales in fiscal 2025 and 16% in fiscal 2024.
The loss of, or significant adverse change in, our relationship with any of these key retailers could cause our net sales, operating income and cash flow to decline.

business_model.claim: The Cost and Simplicity agenda—covering procurement, logistics, manufacturing, portfolio optimization and administrative functions—has been a key driver of gross margin and operating income improvement, contributing to a 240-basis-point gross margin expansion in fiscal 2025 to 31.9% and an operating margin increase to 8.0% from 5.8%.
quotes: Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 31.9% in fiscal 2025 from 29.5% in fiscal 2024.
Our operating margin improved to 8.0% in fiscal 2025 from 5.8% in fiscal 2024.

business_model.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors) and P4 (10-Q MD&A)
business_model.claim: Consumer discretionary spending, weather, and shifts in consumer preferences (including a post-pandemic decline in durable goods demand) are key external drivers of revenue variability across both segments.
quotes: Our sales ultimately depend on consumer discretionary spending, which is influenced by factors beyond our control, including high interest rates, the potential for trade tariffs, a return to an inflationary environment or an economic recession, other general economic conditions, the availability of discretionary income and credit, weather, consumer confidence and unemployment levels.
The decline in Pet net sales was due primarily to lower sales of durable items impacting our outdoor cushions, pet beds and aquatics businesses.

quotes: We are a leader in both the U.S. pet supplies market and the lawn and garden consumables market.

Our diversified portfolio spans many of the most recognized brands in their categories, including Aqueon in aquatics, Cadet in dog treats and chews, Farnam in equine, Four Paws in waste management and grooming, K&H in heated pet products, Kaytee in pet bird and small animal, and Nylabone in dog toys and treats as well as Amdro in controls, Ferry-Morse in packet seed and Pennington in wild bird products, grass seed and fertilizer.

Home Depot, our second largest customer, represented approximately 16% of total net sales in fiscal 2025 and 17% in fiscal 2024.
Together with Costco, Lowe's and Amazon these major retailers represented approximately 54% of total net sales in fiscal 2025 and 2024.

quotes: Since 1992, we have completed more than 60 acquisitions, building a company with approximately $3.1 billion in net sales.

quotes: Our operating income increased $64.7 million, or 34.9%, to $250.0 million in fiscal 2025.
Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 31.9% in fiscal 2025 from 29.5% in fiscal 2024.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-Q MD&A and 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: In Q3 fiscal 2026, Central's GAAP operating margin improved to 14.3% and non-GAAP operating margin to 15.4%, while gross margin reached 35.9%, reflecting the exit of the lower-margin pet distribution business and ongoing cost initiatives.
quotes: Operating income declined $9 million from the prior year quarter to $126 million and our operating margin improved to 14.3% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. On a non-GAAP basis, operating income declined $3 million and operating margin improved to 15.4% from the prior year quarter.
Gross profit was $317 million, compared with $332 million, a decrease of 5%, with gross margin expanding by 130 basis points to 35.9% from 34.6%.

competitive_position.claim: Central manufactures the majority of its branded products in U.S.-based facilities, supplemented by contract manufacturing and facilities in Canada and Mexico, giving it a scaled, integrated logistics network serving mass-market and independent retail channels.
quotes: We manufacture the majority of our branded products in our U.S.-based facilities, supplemented by select contract manufacturing arrangements, including an exclusive supply of our registered active ingredient (S)-Methoprene. In addition, we operate manufacturing facilities in Canada and Mexico.
Our pet and garden sales and fulfillment facilities are strategically located across the United States, enabling us to serve both mass-market customers and independent pet specialty retail stores.

competitive_position.claim: Central's largest competitors in the Pet segment are Spectrum Brands, Mars, Inc., and the J.M. Smucker Co., and in the Garden segment are Scotts Miracle-Gro, Spectrum Brands, and S.C. Johnson.
quotes: Our largest competitors in the Pet segment are Spectrum Brands, Mars, Inc. and the J.M Smucker Co., and our largest competitors in the Garden segment are Scotts Miracle-Gro, Spectrum Brands and S.C. Johnson.

competitive_position.claim: Key retail customers have increased buying power, are implementing just-in-time purchasing, and are emphasizing private label products, which could reduce Central's branded product sales and increase working capital requirements.
quotes: These key retailers are large and sophisticated with increased buying power and negotiating strength. They are more capable of resisting price increases and can demand lower pricing.

Additionally, some retailers are increasing their emphasis on private label products. These retailers may also in the future use more of their shelf space, currently used for our products, for their store brand products.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors; tariff refunds noted in 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: U.S. tariffs imposed during 2025, ranging from a 10% baseline to much higher rates, threaten to increase Central's input costs, as less than 15% of its cost of goods sold was sourced from outside the United States, primarily from China, Brazil, and Mexico.
quotes: During 2025, the U.S. Administration has imposed significant tariffs on goods imported, ranging from a 10% baseline to much higher rates on a variety of imports.
In fiscal 2025, less than 15% of our cost of goods sold was from products or materials sourced from outside the United States, primarily from China, Brazil and Mexico.

competitive_position.claim: Central's Garden segment is highly seasonal, with approximately 64% of Garden net sales and 57% of total net sales occurring in the second and third fiscal quarters, and is exposed to adverse weather and commodity seed/grain price volatility.
quotes: In fiscal 2025, approximately 64% of our Garden segment's net sales and 57% of our total net sales occurred during our second and third fiscal quarters.

Beginning in fiscal 2023, there has been a prolonged oversupply of grass seed, which has resulted in a significant decline in market prices. As a result of this decline, in fiscal 2024, we incurred an approximately $15-$20 million charge to write-down the value of our grass seed inventory.

competitive_position.claim: Federal and state restrictions on importation of pet birds and small animals have reduced availability and demand for related food and supplies, and a significant avian flu outbreak in the United States would further reduce demand for pet and wild bird food.
quotes: The federal government and many state governments have increased restrictions on the importation of pet birds and the supply of small animals. These restrictions have resulted in reduced availability of new pet birds and small animals and thus reduced demand for pet bird and small animal food and supplies.
A significant outbreak in the United States would reduce demand for our pet and wild bird food and negatively impact our financial results.

competitive_position.claim: The eCommerce channel continues to grow rapidly, and if key brick-and-mortar retailers lose share to eCommerce, Central could lose sales; however, Central is investing to access the digital channel more effectively.
quotes: The eCommerce channel continues to grow rapidly. To the extent that the key retailers, including retailers in the pet specialty segment, on which we depend lose share to the eCommerce channel, we could lose sales.
Pure-play eCommerce players continue to gain share, as younger, digitally-native consumers, now entering prime pet-owning years, outspend older generations.
